what: Wildfire now nine miles away from French city of Bordeaux, mayor warns

clean_source_blocks.text: Thomas Cazenave says they are preparing if further evacuations are issued, as the mayor of a nearby town called the situation "catastrophic".

Meanwhile in Spain, 25,000 people have been ordered to evacuate and almost 40,000 have been told to stay indoors. Wildfires near Madrid "slowed their advance" overnight but remain active, the regional government said today. The Prince and Princess of Wales have also offered their condolences to those affected by the wildfires, which they claim are a “stark reminder of the challenges posed by an increasingly extreme climate”. The mayor of Bordeaux says that wildfire is now nine miles from the city and that he braced for "all eventualities". Thomas Cazenave said: "We are preparing to accommodate a large number of people should further evacuations be ordered." France’s Interior Ministry says 13,566 fires have swept across over 116,000 hectares (448 square miles) since January, the highest annual figure in the country’s modern records.

Firefighters in Gironde are facing an "unprecedented" situation as they battle a blaze that "has a life of its own", the interior minister has warned The mayor of Bordeaux has said he is bracing for "all eventualities", as one of many wildfires raging in France is now 15km (nine miles) from the south-western city. "We are preparing to accommodate a large number of people should further evacuations be ordered," said Thomas Cazenave. Firefighters in the Gironde region were facing an "unprecedented" situation battling a fire that "has a life of its own", said Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez. Some 220,000 people have been evacuated in France and more than 100,000 in Spain, where fires are burning "uncontrolled" west of Madrid. Another intense heatwave on Tuesday could further hamper firefighting efforts.

Jerome Steffe, the mayor of Cestas, a town south of Bordeaux, told the BBC this "will be the fire of the century". He described how 17,000 residents were evacuated from his town during the night when the fire swelled two days ago. So far, he said, the region has seen 42,000 hectares (103,000 acres) of land burned and 240 houses destroyed. "In my city the situation is really catastrophic," he added. And although the fire is no longer moving as quickly, he said his teams have "won only a small battle" and emphasised that the risk remains from flying embers or a sudden change in wind direction. "We put all our energy into creating protective firebreaks," he explained, but admitted "we are all scared in front of this situation."

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has warned the country "is going through an unprecedented fire season".

In a post on X on Monday, Lecornu wrote that "116,085 hectares [286,852 acres] have already burned and 13,566 fire starts have been recorded since January".

The minister revealed that nine out of 10 fires "are human-caused and most arise from carelessness: a cigarette butt, a barbecue, work carried out without precaution".

But he also said that "not all these fires are accidents" and "some are deliberately set", adding that since 6 July, 162 arrests have taken place.

President Emmanuel Macron is now visiting some of the fire-ravaged areas in Gironde to show his support for firefighters and other teams responding to the blazes.

Wildfires are also burning in several other French regions, including Var and Landes, and also in Haute-Corse on the island of Corsica.

An 'unprecedented' wildfire raging seven miles from the French city of Bordeaux has been labelled the 'fire of the century' by its mayor, as fears grow that it could take months to contain.

Firefighters are struggling to contain the flames, which have burned 42,000 hectares - an area four times the size of Paris - leaving two firefighters dead and 88 injured. Volunteers, including local farmers, are helping by towing huge water tankers to the scene.

President Emmanuel Macron held a crisis meeting today as shifting winds and arid conditions have made the blaze difficult to control. France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the blaze has a "life of its own," and is behaving in "in a completely erratic manner" that makes it difficult to control.

Meanwhile in Spain, 25,000 people have been ordered to evacuate and almost 40,000 have been told to stay indoors. Wildfires near Madrid "slowed their advance" overnight but remain active, the regional government said today.

The Prince and Princess of Wales have also offered their condolences to those affected by the wildfires, which they claim are a “stark reminder of the challenges posed by an increasingly extreme climate”.

The mayor of Bordeaux says that wildfire is now nine miles from the city and that he braced for "all eventualities".

Thomas Cazenave said: "We are preparing to accommodate a large number of people should further evacuations be ordered."

France’s Interior Ministry says 13,566 fires have swept across over 116,000 hectares (448 square miles) since January, the highest annual figure in the country’s modern records.

A series of aerial photos of the town La Porge have captured the scale of devastation wrought by the wildfires as they continue to rage throughout the outskirts of Bordaeux.

After several days of uninterrupted spread of the massive wildfire on the outskirts of Bordeaux, the situation remained generally stable overnight(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

This aerial view shows damaged houses in a burnt area in the town of Le Porge,(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

This aerial picture shows smoke billowing from a forested area near Le Porge, in southwestern France(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A fire in Gros Bessillon, in the Var region of southeast France is "still dynamic, unpredictable," and "far from contained ," says Prefect Simon Babre.

The fire has intensified this afternoon on the seventh day that emergency services have been tackling it.
